description: The official Mass Mobilization version, universe, schema, and license are not verified. The local manual copy is a May 2015 codebook; the additional Coding Procedure is missing.
required_followup: Coordinator should resolve the official baseline and missing procedure before coding decisions are treated as official.

description: The open-web search engine is not a substitute for the historical LexisNexis workflow. Results were pooled across four-query calls and exposed no per-query mapping or verified total.
required_followup: If available, use systematic newspaper archives and retain query-level result metadata. Do not infer exhaustive coverage from this first pass.

description: The first pass used English and Lao-script searches plus selected Thai, Chinese, and Vietnamese queries, but it did not systematically search local Lao archives or independently verify translations.
required_followup: Search additional Lao-language local outlets and archived local reporting; verify any translated event claims against accessible originals.

description: Several potentially relevant pages were inaccessible: State Department reports returned forbidden, BHRRC returned HTTP 403, and LaoNews failed at local DNS resolution before an HTTP response.
required_followup: Use only ordinary authorized access if these same public URLs become reachable; do not bypass access controls. Keep blocked and local-network failures distinct.

description: RFA reports affected households in two land-compensation accounts but does not report a simultaneous public assembly or attendees; household totals cannot establish the 50-person threshold.
required_followup: Look for independent contemporaneous evidence of an actual public meeting or gathering and its attendance before proposing either as an event.

description: The Guestown-Lao reporting says workers approached for back pay in December and January but does not establish that those contacts were public gatherings or demands to the Lao state; the documented assembly occurred in February and targeted a private owner.
required_followup: February-unit reviewer may inspect the original April RFA report and any earlier source to establish what “came here several times” refers to, whether any group assembled, and the addressee.

description: No qualifying physical protest beginning in December 2020 and continuing into January was established. The Guestown-Lao article mentions earlier wage approaches but not public gatherings; the Feb. 22 gathering is owned by February.
required_followup: Check December and February neighbor units for independently documented starts or continuations; do not assign the February assembly to January without evidence of a qualifying January onset.

description: Political restrictions on public reporting and uneven access to local and diaspora sources make source-indexed silence especially weak evidence. The October 2020 hashtag discussion does not identify a verified physical location for overseas posters or an overseas meeting.
required_followup: Seek event-specific records that establish physical location, date, and target for any diaspora action. Do not treat online activity or poster origin as a gathering.

description: Several secondary items repeat the same source chain: FIDH and BHRRC refer to RFA’s Jan. 29 land report; RFA’s April and May wage items are one agency chain; The China Project cites local press and RFA for the separate 2022 Khammouane episode.
required_followup: Trace original reporting and bylines before treating repeated publication as independent corroboration.
